name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply formatting-only patches to third-party dependencies.

Formatting patches are low-risk, high-value: they change only whitespace and line breaks, never logic. This keeps our codebase consistent without touching behavior, reducing merge conflicts and review load. The trade-off is accepting occasional noise in dependency diffs, but the benefit of uniform style outweighs it.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t just "skipping deeper logic fixes"—it’s that formatting-only patches mask the real problem: inconsistent tooling. A better alternative is to enforce formatting standards *before* code lands in the repo, not after. Settle this by running a controlled test: apply formatting to one dependency, measure merge conflict rates and review time over two sprints.
